captions.linkedin:
December winners win December again. Most quants throw this signal in the trash. 📊

Heston and Sadka (2008, JFE) ran a regression nobody else bothered to run. They lagged stock returns by 12, 24, 36, all the way out to 240 months. Coefficients were positive at every annual lag.

In plain English: the stock that beat its peers last January tends to beat them next January too. Same for every month. The pattern survives controls for size, industry, January effect, dividends and earnings.

Most people dismiss this as the January effect, or noise. It isn't. It's a stock-level calendar pattern that runs alongside size, value, and momentum.

Here's the complete logic. No black box:

🔹 SAME-MONTH SIGNAL, compute each stock's average return in the target month over 10-20 years.
🔹 DECILE RANKING, sort by that historical same-month performance.
🔹 LONG TOP DECILE, hold for 1 month.
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE, re-rank for the next calendar slot.
🔹 INTERNATIONAL, documented in multiple markets.

Likely drivers: seasonal cash flows, risk exposures, or behavioral calendar anchoring. Pick your story. The signal is the signal.

If you already run momentum, this is an orthogonal calendar signal that combines cleanly.
